approach.method_basis: The Parent evolves molecular graphs from accepted, scored molecules. It samples high-ranked breeding parents, recombines connected fragments and applies local mutations and occasional successive mutations; direct aromatic carbon/nitrogen exchange is already disabled. Stable identity checks form a fresh surplus pool. An accepted-only Gaussian process represents molecules by counts of local Morgan environments and uses generalized Tanimoto similarity. Its correlated posterior score draws allocate the next evaluations, and accepted offspring update the full prediction archive and the bounded breeding population.
approach.novelty: Remove environment multiplicity from the predictor by replacing each cached count vector with binary presence in exactly the same molecular vocabulary. Keep the shared kernel equation, fitting settings and correlated allocation rule. This is a reverse control on the current exchange-free Parent: earlier count variants improved the mean on an exchange-enabled search, while narrowing intervals and worsening coverage, and they repeated the same trajectories. No evaluated same-Parent child in this brief has tested the representation removal. The pending correlation and mean-only controls retain count features and change allocation instead. This experiment asks whether count information still supports endpoint search, with a predicted loss when it is removed; any replay of an older binary search will be identified explicitly.

observed_bottleneck: The unresolved behavior in n-62daf219c70a is its dependence on occurrence-weighted molecular similarity after aromatic exchange was removed. The Parent actual per-seed summaries and run logs are complete, with macro mean 0.5956696497334577, population SD 0.02659287062806747 and seed macros 0.625411930168826, 0.560865654270234 and 0.600731364761313. Its source uses one count-feature cache for accepted training, fresh-pool prediction and next-fit probes. Reading all fifteen task logs finds repeated training bins in every one of 435 fits, with 65,250 training-row occurrences, 737,030 logged bins above one across those fits, 69,600 pooled occurrences and 4,350 correlated sampled choices. These are exposed count computations, not an endpoint contribution estimate. The original indexed reports for n-559d25e9c9c7 and n-98e8cdf5c51d show that counts changed all 435 fitted pool distributions and 434 same-normal selected batches relative to binary features on n-9edaa26007c3. Their shared historical macro gain was 0.022573281535690642, with one seed decline, while latent 1.96-SD coverage fell from about 85.63% to 76.92% and exact fingerprint ties persisted. All fifteen archived trajectory pairs for those two count variants are byte-identical, so this is one trajectory panel, not two independent successes. The catalog still leaves component contribution unresolved. Historical exchange removal n-c55c3d520a2c then changed the composition and improved its mean; n-62daf219c70a reproduced that exchange-free source and trajectories under the current profile without identifying a retained component effect. Historical binary ancestor n-213e85380e04 has the same inherited feature vocabulary and no direct exchange route, but its source differs in passive tracing and kernel expression; inspection makes possible behavior equivalence worth checking, not established by equal scores or wording. The limitation being tested is unisolated count-dependent weighting, not evidence that counts failed to execute or that worse interval coverage necessarily harmed endpoint search.
hypothesis: Remove Morgan environment multiplicity from the shared posterior representation by replacing each inherited count vector c with binary presence 1[c > 0] for every training, pool and next-fit feature use, while retaining the generalized Tanimoto implementation and all fitting, graph-generation and correlated-allocation rules.

finding_summary.headline: Removing environment counts lowers the matched mean by 0.051296 and reproduces the earlier binary search
finding_summary.insights: The isolated reverse control supports a positive contribution of environment multiplicity in the current exchange-free composition. It changes both fitted means and covariance, so the experiment does not assign the gain specifically to calibrated uncertainty. More structural variety is also insufficient: binary selection yields 2,267 typed and 1,546 generic cores versus 1,851 and 1,118 under counts, yet strict local parent beats fall from 629 to 565 and incumbent gains from 258 to 218. Molecular evidence preserves the useful conventional ketone and aminoaryl-dione gains alongside reactive environments, repeated large assemblies and destructive fragments; no universal size or chemistry rule explains the score loss. The fifteen trajectories and all shared non-timing decisions exactly reproduce the earlier binary ancestor. That establishes provenance and rules out treating the replay as new independent evidence; the current matched Parent comparison remains the contribution test. Which changes in similarity, means and covariance mediate the useful search behavior remains open.
finding_summary.results: Every active feature is binary under extensive repeated-environment exposure, and all 435 fitted pools change their posterior relative to counts on the same inputs. The retained correlated draws, graph operations and accepted feedback reconstruct correctly. Mean final score falls from 0.595670 to 0.544374, a paired loss of 0.051296 against the registered 0.002 scale. All seed macros decline: 0.077877, 0.002003 and 0.074008. Twelve task-seed endpoints decline; zaleplon_mpo improves on seed 0, while deco_hop and sitagliptin_mpo improve on seed 1. On the actual binary stream, latent 1.96-SD coverage is 79.75% versus 73.52% for a passive count model using the same earlier labels and scored molecules. Their MSEs are 0.016600/0.009873. Binary error is higher in all fifteen task-seed cells, while its coverage is lower for median_2 on every seed despite the aggregate increase. These diagnostics answer a different question from endpoint search utility.

molecular.headline: Compact ketone and aminoaryl-dione leaders coexist with reactive heterocycles, repeated large assemblies and low-scoring fragments
molecular.overall_character: All fifteen Child and fifteen published Parent trajectory files were present and read. Every task has 900 records and 870 optimizer proposals across Search Seeds 0, 1 and 2; tasks_without_trajectories is empty. The brief reports complete Child evaluation and complete profile-matched pairing with code Parent n-62daf219c70a, with no profile-mismatched seeds. The Parent comparisons below therefore use the complete published current-profile panel. This report describes chemistry and its observed score associations; it does not judge activation or attribute individual structural changes to the feature-representation intervention. The output remains rich in rings and aromatic frameworks: ring-closure-string incidence spans 0.9736 to 0.9943, and aromatic-string incidence 0.9414 to 0.9885. These counters measure presence in a molecule, not perceived ring count, aromatic-atom fraction or useful scaffold diversity. The molecules include compact annulated ketones, nitrogen/sulfur-containing spiro and bridged systems, linked heteroaromatic carbonyl assemblies, aryl-containing basic amines, medium/large nitrogen-carbonyl rings and fluorinated fused diones. Families differ across seeds, but leaders often remain close relatives within a seed, supporting moderate overall structural diversity. Some conspicuous leaders have comparatively conventional local chemistry: the ketone/fluoropyridyl family and an aminomethyl/fluoroalkyl aryl-dione family improve their matched Parent scores without N-F bonds. The strongest aryl-amine examples also use ordinary carbon-bound halogens. These counterexamples prevent a claim that reactive heteroatom-halogen chemistry is unavoidable. Nevertheless, other leaders contain N-F/N-Cl, peroxide-halogen chains, cyanates, aldehydes, chloromethyl ethers or crowded nitrogen/sulfur bridges. Large repeated aryl/dione assemblies and tiny poor-scoring fragments occur alongside the compact families. Synthetic plausibility remains questionable and overall drug-likeness weak; the visible conventional examples do not validate the complete set. Formal-charge and stereocentre-string incidences are 0.0 for all tasks, despite protonatable amines and potentially stereogenic saturated centres. Heavy-atom sizes below were counted from the cited trajectory SMILES tokens; geometry, synthesis and physical properties were not validated. The digest final excerpts are late seed-2 proposals, and some final proposals are poor fragments or truncated analogues despite a better retained incumbent. Parent statements use its published trajectories; cited_smiles contains only current molecules allowed by the digest or trusted citation paths.

per_task.generated_character: The seed-0 leader has 24 heavy atoms and an ethyl/methyl-substituted annulated nitrogen/oxygen aromatic framework bearing a ketone-linked fluoropyridylmethyl group. Its fluorine is carbon-bound; it has no N-halogen or O-F bond. A nearby high scorer instead has a fluorophenyl ketone on a related annulated nitrogen/oxygen framework. Seed 1 reaches a 25-heavy-atom crowded nitrogen/sulfur ring system with lactam/imine functionality and a vinyl thioether; seed 2 reaches a 25-heavy-atom expanded nitrogen-ring carboxanilide with N-F and an N-N bond. Mean proposal SMILES length is 44.5, with halogen incidence 0.869. The strongest family is compact and more conventional locally than the N-halogen series, though its annulation and N/O-containing ring still require a practical synthesis and stability assessment.
liabilities: The seed-1 leader combines N-S connectivity, imine/lactam and vinyl-thioether functionality in a crowded ring system; the seed-2 leader retains N-F and N-N bonds.
The top ketone family is a real counterexample to obligatory reactive halogen placement, but ring connectivity and any relevant stereochemical identity remain unvalidated.
Late halogen and hydrocarbon fragments lose essentially all of the useful aromatic/carbonyl context.
missing_features: Conventional compact alternatives are not reached consistently across seeds: the successful ketone family avoids N-halogen chemistry, while other leading families retain reactive linker or crowded ring environments.
Independent plausible ways of retaining the favorable aromatic/carbonyl relationship are less evident among leading relatives than peripheral and local ring edits.
Configurations and accessible geometry of annulated and sulfur/nitrogen-rich centres are unresolved; lower scoring unrelated seeds do not prove that a particular missing bond or atom is required.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial trimethoxyindole anilide scores 0.3051048083696145. The annulated fluoropyridylmethyl ketone reaches 0.4463521672202675, and the related fluorophenyl ketone 0.4349635367667153. These observations associate the compact aromatic/carbonyl organization with useful scores without requiring an amide or an N-halogen bond. The Child seed-0 leader exceeds the Parent cumulene-containing leader at 0.39405142067435733. Seed-1 and seed-2 leaders score 0.4126819838532174 and 0.4163503402962837, below Parent 0.47411701813450596 and 0.438972502037081. Isolated fluorine and late ethene score 0.0, so ring/linker context matters and halogen presence alone is insufficient. The final seed-2 ethene does not replace its higher incumbent. The observations do not identify a missing exact target pharmacophore.

per_task.generated_character: The seed-1 leader has 32 heavy atoms and links fused nitrogen/oxygen carbonyl heterocycles through an NH group, with aromatic bromine, an O-linked cyanate and an O-O-Cl substituent. Its ring system includes additional compact carbon bridging. Seed 0 instead reaches a 65-heavy-atom multiaryl assembly containing repeated nitrogen-rich dione regions, vinyl substituents, carbonyls and aryl bromine. Seed 2 reaches a 38-heavy-atom extensively annulated/linking nitrogen-dione assembly with N-F, N-Cl and haloalkyl substitution. Mean proposal SMILES length is 94.4 and its maximum is 248, documenting extensive growth elsewhere in the proposal set. The compact seed-1 framework and much larger seed-0 assembly are chemically distinct; neither ring abundance nor repeated dione motifs ensures a useful or plausible arrangement.
liabilities: O-O-Cl and O-O-F connections in near-leaders combine peroxide and oxygen-halogen chemistry; they are not ordinary aryl chlorides or fluorides.
The O-linked cyanate differs chemically from a carbon-linked nitrile. Other seed leaders contain N-halogen bonds and haloalkyl groups.
Large repeated aryl/dione assemblies add substantial complexity without uniformly higher scores, while small fragments lose the ring-and-linker arrangement entirely.
missing_features: Stable alternatives to peroxide-halogen and O-linked cyanate functionality that preserve the compact favorable linked-heterocycle arrangement are not demonstrated at the leader's score.
The large repeated assemblies do not demonstrate the compact functional-group organization achieved by the strongest Parent examples.
Practical geometry, route and stereochemical identity of the compact bridges remain unresolved; no exact missing target decoration can be inferred.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial aryl-substituted dione scores 0.548381482770623. The compact seed-1 leader reaches 0.6324703199409752, while a related less bridged variant scores 0.6309644029285534. This supports a retained combined heterocyclic organization more strongly than an absolute requirement for that particular bridge. Its score exceeds the matched Parent leader at 0.6248206599713055, but the O-O-Cl and cyanate liabilities remain. Seed 0 reaches only 0.6004556752278376 with 65 heavy atoms, compared with the Parent's 30-heavy-atom leader at 0.8561477222467935. Seed 2 reaches 0.6083454583246726 versus Parent 0.6178024026512013. Tiny methylamine and halogen fragments sit at 0.5. The gradient supports neither indiscriminate growth nor a fixed size cutoff: the higher seed-1 score and lower seed-0 score arise in different organizations.

per_task.generated_character: The seed-2 leader has 31 heavy atoms and combines an aryl-containing secondary amine with a substituted alkene and a nitrogen-rich cyclic aminal bearing an exocyclic amino group and a difluorophenyl substituent. The seed-0 leader is a smaller 27-heavy-atom diazaspirocycle with aryl bromine/chlorine, an arylethyl N-substituent and a phenyl thiol. These leading structures contain carbon-bound halogens rather than N-F or O-F. Seed 1 reaches a 31-heavy-atom crowded bridged tertiary amine with an aniline connection, chloromethyl ether, aldehyde and mercaptomethyl group. Mean proposal SMILES length is 60.2 and halogen incidence 0.9874. Available aliphatic amines and aromatic surfaces are already prominent; the concerns are molecular organization, aminal stability, local reactive groups and unresolved stereochemistry.
liabilities: The leading cyclic aminal has a carbon attached to several nitrogens; its stability is not established by its score. The recognizable diazaspirocycle offers a different chemistry counterexample.
Other leaders contain thiol, aldehyde and chloromethyl-ether environments; near-leading spiro variants also contain O-Cl bonds.
The basic and aromatic regions can be lost together in very poor late proposals, despite retention of one nitrogen-rich ring.
missing_features: The saturated aminal and spiro/bridged amine arrangements lack explicit stereochemical identity and demonstrated accessible conformations.

Stable alternatives retaining the favorable aromatic/basic arrangement are not demonstrated consistently across seeds; the strongest examples already avoid heteroatom-halogen bonds, so blanket halogen removal is unsupported.
Protonation representation is unresolved in the neutral strings, but the output does not lack basic amines.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: An early aryl-amide/carboxylic-acid proposal scores 0.000719339566735797 and a small halogenated aromatic fragment 0.001421581552029289. The seed-2 aryl/amine/cyclic-aminal leader reaches 0.9914038363125457. A late shortened N-O-containing analogue missing one aryl-alkyl region scores 0.011495655106721757; this compound changes both connectivity and functionality, so it supports a context requirement without isolating one atom's contribution. A formylated/reconnected nitrogen analogue scores 0.48797702544581545, while another local variant retaining the larger aryl-amine organization scores 0.989167131859766. Seed-0 and seed-1 leaders score 0.9908331648929692 and 0.9512348232667347. All remain below their matched Parent values of 0.9999989177995104, 0.9969753164881906 and 0.9999934235240012. The visible positive association is the arrangement of available amines with aromatic regions; these scores are not measured affinity or selectivity.

per_task.generated_character: The seed-0 leader has 31 heavy atoms: an alkyl-substituted pyridine connected to a partly saturated nitrogen-containing ring fused into an aromatic dicarbonyl system, with an N-methyl amine. Seed 1 reaches a 35-heavy-atom diaryl/bridged nitrogen-carbonyl system containing N-F. Seed 2 reaches a 28-heavy-atom hydroxyquinoline linked by methylene to a larger unsaturated nitrogen-dicarbonyl ring. Mean proposal SMILES length is 55.9 and halogen incidence 0.269. Aromatic regions, carbonyls and amines are all present, but medium/large rings and bridge connectivity lack a demonstrated synthesis or conformational assignment. The families resemble the Parent's broad aromatic/nitrogen-carbonyl territory without reproducing its exact leaders.
liabilities: Larger nitrogen rings and aromatic-fused junctions create geometric and synthetic questions despite recognizable amine and carbonyl groups.
One seed leader contains N-F, while potential stereogenic centres in multiple families have no explicit assignments.
Both near-empty fragments and larger duplicated aromatic systems appear at poor scores, so a single universal size rule would miss the observed context dependence.
missing_features: The leading families do not establish accessible simpler connectivities reproducing the favorable arrangement at the Parent scores.
Conformational and stereochemical identity of the medium/large rings and crowded junctions remains unspecified.
Useful functional-group context is not reliably preserved when simplifying or enlarging these structures; neither more heteroatoms nor an extra aromatic copy is shown to be a general solution.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial aryl-substituted dione scores 0.1678386594791329. The seed-0 pyridine/annulated-dicarbonyl leader reaches 0.22405709718343647, and a nearby nitrogen/ring-connectivity variant scores 0.22071211094442214. Seed-1 and seed-2 leaders reach 0.2133697489012744 and 0.21037674112349405. All remain below Parent 0.2258403994203931, 0.2214095461892601 and 0.22600312875247064, respectively, with the first pair especially close. A late seed-2 structure with two quinoline regions and 41 heavy atoms scores 0.1754730092490373, below its 28-heavy-atom leader; duplicating an aromatic motif is not sufficient. Atomic sulfur and ClCl score 0.0. The observed gradient favors a combined aromatic/nitrogen/carbonyl arrangement over isolated fragments or indiscriminate repetition, without identifying an exact absent target motif.

per_task.generated_character: The seed-1 leader has 27 heavy atoms and a comparatively conventional fused N-methyl/N-fluoromethyl dione attached to a phenyl ring bearing aminomethyl, aryl fluorine and fluoromethyl groups. All its fluorines are carbon-bound; it contains no N-F or O-F and no small cyclic cumulene. Seed 0 instead reaches a 24-heavy-atom difluorinated nitrogen heteroaromatic bearing formyl/urea/imino functionality and an unsaturated oxygen-containing ring. Seed 2 reaches a 28-heavy-atom fused nitrogen-dione/aza-aromatic system with hydroxyl, mercaptomethyl and a substituted fluorocyclopropyl group. Mean proposal SMILES length is 53.0; cumulated-double-bond incidence is 0.0483 across the full proposal set, although the best seed-1 molecule has none. The strongest family is recognizable aromatic amine/dione chemistry, while other seeds retain more crowded or unusual topology.
liabilities: Some nearby high scorers retain N-F despite its absence from the top molecule; the top provides a counterexample to a universal reactive-halogen requirement.

Other seed families contain densely fused rings, imino/formyl-rich arrangements, thiol-containing substitution or small unsaturated rings. These must be assessed individually, rather than treating ordinary fluorocyclopropyl or carbon-bound fluorine as intrinsically implausible.

Very large repeated dione/aryl assemblies reach extremely poor scores, while sharp score changes occur among compact molecules of similar appearance. Size and motif presence alone do not capture the observed relationship.
missing_features: The output does not consistently reach the favorable conventional aminoalkyl/fluorinated-dione organization across seeds, even though its own leading examples demonstrate that capability.

Stable, independent arrangements that preserve the favorable local functional-group relationships at the stronger Parent scores remain unestablished; the scores do not reveal a required exact target scaffold.
Stereochemical definition of substituted small rings and tautomeric/conformational definition of the more unusual nitrogen-rich systems are unresolved.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The seed-1 leader reaches 0.5845583988949146 versus its Parent's 0.4870057305679067, an important gain without reactive N-F chemistry. A close analogue changes aminomethyl to nitrile and scores 0.3127382806635915; replacing one aryl fluoromethyl by directly attached fluorine gives 0.33665072792737094. Replacing an aryl fluorine by amino gives 0.008531806861625604. These direct comparisons support coordinated aminoalkyl and fluorinated substituent placement in that scaffold, not indiscriminate addition of nitrogen or fluorine. An earlier 60-heavy-atom linked dione assembly scores 1.6758614448245604e-53. Seed 0 reaches 0.4759777345546235 and seed 2 0.4071395189354175, below Parent 0.6510211907030741 and 0.7208853668418119. The seed-2 fluorocyclopropyl leader becomes a lower-scoring 0.3862488109868912 relative after a ring-unsaturation/topology change; neither that nor the Parent's cyclic-cumulene leader establishes that strained unsaturation is required. The best local score gain therefore accompanies a plausible alternative family, while other seeds remain below the Parent.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Observed in n-e00db808bbb4 on Search Seeds 0, 1 and 2 at 300 observations per task, with complete current-profile Parent n-62daf219c70a. The environment gap previously recorded in n-c55c3d520a2c persists through N-halogen, oxygen-oxygen-halogen, cyanate, aldehyde and chloromethyl-ether chemistry. Counterexamples are especially important here: a compact ketone family and a conventional aminoaryl-dione family improve matched Parent scores without N-F, and the strongest aryl-amine examples use carbon-bound halogens. Thus reactivity is conditional on local environment and is not unavoidable for useful output.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not consistently retain conventional bond environments while exploring useful aromatic and polar arrangements.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Task-agnostic transformations need plausible local alternatives preserving feedback-supported functional-group relationships, while distinguishing ordinary carbon-bound halogens, amides, ethers and amines from reactive bond patterns. Preserve and explore the demonstrated conventional alternatives. The evidence does not prove that a blanket filter improves score or attribute any specific liability to the feature representation.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Source n-e00db808bbb4 under complete paired Search conditions with n-62daf219c70a, continuing the context/coverage gap first recorded in n-c55c3d520a2c. Current output contains a 65-heavy-atom repeated aryl/dione leader below its matched 30-heavy-atom Parent, a 60-heavy-atom assembly at an extremely low score, and a 41-heavy-atom doubled aromatic variant below its 28-heavy-atom relative. Tiny late fragments and truncated aryl-amine analogues also score poorly. Counterexamples include compact conventional families that improve their matched endpoints and substantial rings that retain useful scores; neither growth nor simplification is uniformly beneficial.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not reliably preserve useful molecular context while controlling repeated elaboration and destructive simplification.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Use task-local feedback to test independent connectivities and simplifications that preserve useful aromatic, carbonyl and basic-region relationships, rather than treating repeated motifs or fewer atoms as sufficient. The missing capability is consistent preservation of functional context, not an inability to form rings or large molecules. No fixed size cutoff, repetition ban or component-level causal claim follows from this chemistry.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Source n-e00db808bbb4 on the supplied complete Search panel and profile, compared with n-62daf219c70a. Leaders contain nitrogen/sulfur bridges, spirocycles, carbon centres attached to several nitrogens, larger nitrogen-carbonyl rings and compact fused diones. Ring text remains prevalent throughout. The earlier geometry concern from n-c55c3d520a2c persists in changed structures, while a conventional aminoaryl-dione and a recognizable diazaspirocycle are counterexamples to a uniformly implausible output. The Parent's particular cyclic-cumulene leader is not a property of the current best family.
transferable_gaps.gap: The output does not consistently establish geometric and synthetic feasibility for crowded annulations, aminal centres and larger nitrogen rings.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Topology changes need environment-sensitive assessment of ring connectivity, unsaturation, aminal stability and accessible conformations, with alternative structures preserving learned useful arrangements. Ring counts and aromatic text cannot establish feasibility. Preserve conventional small and spiro rings where appropriate; this evidence does not establish that all unusual topology is impossible or that geometric filtering necessarily raises reward.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Source n-e00db808bbb4 across all supplied Search Seeds at 300 observations per task, continuing the identity gap recorded in n-c55c3d520a2c and Parent n-62daf219c70a. Every task has stereocentre-string and formal-charge-string incidence 0.0, although substituted saturated rings, spiro/bridged structures and aminoalkyl centres can have stereochemical distinctions. Clear primary, secondary and tertiary amines remain present, so neutral strings do not establish a lack of protonatable chemistry. The comparatively conventional leading dione does not remove the issue from the other generated families.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator leaves relevant stereochemical and molecular-state identity unspecified after producing saturated and heteroatom-rich structures.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Representations and transformations need to preserve or deliberately resolve relevant stereochemistry, with separate assessment of protonation, tautomerism and imine/alkene configuration. Distinguish achiral or configurationally labile structures from those needing stable stereoisomer assignment. These observations establish incomplete chemical identity, not a measured state-dependent score penalty or proof that adding charge or enumeration improves the objective.

method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.

branches: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
retained_mechanisms: Accepted-only task-local GP archive, bounded greedy survivors and score-quantile breeding parents.
Connected-fragment crossover and optional post-crossover mutation; ordinary one-/two-/three-call mutation continuation with the complete saturation/retry law.
All seven ordinary atom/bond/ring mutation families, fixed weights and atom bounds; aromatic C/N exchanges remain disabled with passive opportunity tracing.
Sanitization, stable canonical identity and original-graph reuse, initial/emitted and temporary-pool duplicate rejection, bounded attempts and fixed surplus pools.
The same hashed Morgan vocabulary and shared cache, now active binary presence; shared generalized Tanimoto equation, normalization, fixed noise, finite checks and jitter schedule.
Full posterior covariance, nonzero correlated residuals, inherited random-array call and masks/ties, identity-bound predictions, pending joins and next-fit probes.
Fresh objective-local state, prepared CONFIG and fixed batches/budgets/resources; numerical fallback and generation recovery remain source-preserved but unexercised.
